summary: Michael L. Walter (1947–2020) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Larry William Moses. He served as a research fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1982, 2020).

Michael Lessman specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned a BA from Georgetown University (2010–2014) and MAs from the Catholic University of America (2014–2017) and the University of Munich (2017–2019), before becoming a doctoral candidate at Yale University in 2019.

Michael M. Ames (1933–2006) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1952–1956) and Harvard (~1956–1961) under Cora Du Bois. He taught at McMaster and UBC, later directing the UBC Museum of Anthropology (1974–1997).
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Meier-Brügger (born 1948) is a linguist who studied at the University of Zurich under Ernst Risch (~1968–1973). He later held a post at the Free University of Berlin from around 1994 to 2013.

Michael Oppitz (born 1942) is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He held a post at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as director at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).
Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Pakenham Edgeworth (1812–1881) was an Indology scholar who attended Charterhouse School and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1827–1830). He served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1831 to 1859.

Michael Puett (born 1964) works in Sinology, history/archaeology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1994) under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, subsequently holding professorships at Harvard University (~1994, ~2013).

Michael Pye (born 1939) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds under Maurice Wiles, he taught at Leeds and Lancaster, was a professor at Marburg (1982–2004), and held a visiting professorship at Otani University (~2004–2007).

Michael Radich is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned degrees from Auckland and Harvard, and studied at Kyoto. He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and Heidelberg University (2018), alongside visiting appointments at Kyoto and Hamburg.
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

Michael Schmidt is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held several posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008), the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), and the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992).

Michael Schonken works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an MS from California State University, Fullerton, taught at Beijing Royal School and Nord Anglia School Beijing, and became a PhD student at Tsinghua University in 2024.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (2018).
Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist who attended Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (~1962–1971). He held a post at the University of Chicago from around 1970 to 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker is a Sinology and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held posts at MPIWG, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and was a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Copenhagen under Johannsen, Hammerich, and Westergaard. He worked at the Copenhagen University Library and served as a professor at Copenhagen from 1878 to 1902.

Michael W. Charney (born 1967) is an Asian and military historian who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999. In 2001, he took up a post as Professor of Asian and Military History at SOAS University of London.
